dedupe_keys.name: fjord5g 5g measurements on ferries for coastal maritime connectivity kiel fjord

description: Fjord5G, published by Birkan Denizer and Olaf Landsiedel of Kiel University and presented at the IEEE Vehicular Technology Conference in spring 2025, is a dataset of cellular measurements taken on research and public ferries in the Kiel Fjord in Germany. Four 5G routers on two ferries logged GPS-located network conditions of two mobile network operators once per second for up to twelve months per router, covering signal strength, modulation, bandwidth and related metrics along the maritime routes. Coverage: Kiel Fjord, coastal and near-shore waters of northern Germany, up to a year. Format and access: four compressed Parquet files (about 2.7 GB) on Zenodo with Jupyter notebooks on GitHub, free of charge under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: one fjord and two operators; routers on ferries, not handsets; weather and season effects must be separated by users. Simulation uses: mobile coverage and quality at sea near the coast for the dependence of shipping, ports and offshore operations on terrestrial networks, and resilience of maritime communication. Related records: the Czech railway corridor measurements give a land transport counterpart; the Laura Bassi dataset covers satellite navigation at sea.
